text:
jamie_devex: FYI onboarding sample app failing on Windows 3.11 when customers use a corporate HTTP proxy + venv. Async client raises ssl.SSLCertVerificationError intermittently. Stacktrace below and a tiny repro. Anyone seen this pattern?

jamie_devex: repro steps: pip install -r samples/requirements.txt, activate venv, set HTTPS_PROXY, run samples/async_chat.py

jamie_devex: stack (trimmed):
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:XXXXX)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ConnectionError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/chat (Caused by SSLError(SSLError("[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] ..."))))
```

sara_winqa: ugh, corporate proxy + Windows cert store + venv quirks. Do you have REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE set? Also which OpenSSL shipped with that Python build?

jamie_devex: no env vars set. Python 3.11.4 from official installer. Repro on fresh Win11 machine and on a user's corp laptop. Works fine on mac/linux.

matt_py_sdk: pinging @jamie_devex — can you paste the minimal async snippet? I want to try locally.

jamie_devex: sure:
```python
# async_chat.py (minimal)
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="x", timeout=10)
    await c.chat.create("hello")

asyncio.run(main())
```

sara_winqa: I bet the venv's ssl module isn't picking up the Windows CA store when a corporate proxy intercepts TLS (MITM). Two quick workarounds that helped me: 1) pip install certifi && set SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())") 2) pip install certifi-win32 (it patches win32-certstore to certifi)

olivia_security: heads-up: certifi-win32 is fine but company policy may prefer using the system store directly. We should avoid suggesting packages that bypass policy without approval.

matt_py_sdk: thanks. This looks like two separate issues: (A) CA detection on Windows venvs and (B) retry semantics masking underlying cert verification errors (Max retries exceeded).

matt_py_sdk: proposal: SDK should 1) accept ca_bundle param for both sync and async clients, 2) auto-detect REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE and prefer them, 3) add a clear log message when cert verification fails to avoid opaque "Max retries". Also add doc snippet for Windows + corporate proxy.

jamie_devex: +1. Also typing/compat note: some customers on 3.8 hit typing import errors in our async helper tests (we used typing.TypedDict / Protocol without typing_extensions). Should we backport with typing_extensions in install_requires for py<=3.9?

matt_py_sdk: yes, add typing_extensions conditional. I'll open a small PR for the ca_bundle param and better error handling. Quick patch idea: when creating ssl context, if env var set then use cafile param: ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ.get('SSL_CERT_FILE') or certifi.where())

jamie_devex: example workaround we gave customers that worked:
```powershell
python -m pip install certifi certifi-win32
setx SSL_CERT_FILE "$(python -c \"import certifi;print(certifi.where())\")"
# restart terminal/app
```

sara_winqa: one more wrinkle: corporate proxies sometimes require proxy auth and our internal httpx retry logic retries CONNECT failures immediately which triggers proxy to drop connection. We should add jittered backoff for idempotent requests and avoid retrying non-idempotent endpoints by default. Filed an internal ticket for retry policy revamp.

olivia_security: for Private deployments, we should document how to configure KMS and firewall/proxy rules to allow outbound cert verification to work or how to mount CA bundles. Add a short checklist to the onboarding guide.

matt_py_sdk: PR link incoming (WIP) — adds ca_bundle kwarg to AsyncClient, respects SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, pins typing_extensions for older pythons, and improves error text for cert failures. Tests updated to weave in certifi.mock where appropriate.

deploy-bot: new commit pushed to branch fix/win-ca-detect (sha: abc123) :rocket:

jamie_devex: awesome — thanks all. For the immediate support queue I'll paste the workaround and ask affected customers to try certifi-win32 or set SSL_CERT_FILE. I'll follow up on the PR review. :thumbsup:

sara_winqa: also added a tiny flaky test under Windows CI to catch this going forward (3.8-3.12 matrix).

matt_py_sdk: closing loop: feature request to product to expose ca_bundle in our public docs + examples. Filing RFC after PR lands.
